# Kestrel Home: service-request router, final report

*1 October 2026 · repo: github.com/vaibhav375/kestrel-request-router · all numbers regenerated by `evaluate.py`
and the scripts in `experiments/`*

## 1. Summary

Ritu asked for a classifier that matches the vendor bot's labels at 90%. Those labels are the bot's own guesses,
right **77%** of the time. A model that copies them reaches 91.8% agreement and routes no better than the bot.
So the router was trained on **where each request was actually closed**.

| | Vendor bot | **Router** |
|---|---|---|
| Sent to the team that closed it (Apr–Jun 2026, 2,135 unseen requests) | 76.7% | **86.0%** (95% CI 84.5–87.5%) |
| Misrouted requests | 23.3% | **14.0%** (40% fewer) |
| 5-fold cross-validation (10,822 requests) | 77.2% | **86.3% ± 0.2** |
| Macro-F1 | 78.0% | **87.2%** |
| Requests that state a need (84%) | 87.8% | **98.0%** |
| Confident answers auto-routed (84% of volume) | – | **98.4%** right |
| Cost | Rs 3.2 lakh/year (~Rs 38 per request) | **Rs 0 per request** |
| **Saving** | – | **about Rs 8.8 lakh a year** |

**Expected score on the hidden test set:** about **86% accuracy** (range 84–87%); macro-F1 about 87%; about 88% if
scored against the bot's labels.

## 2. What the data showed

* **Payment remarks fool the bot.** Of 626 customers who mentioned paying ("paid on upi"), the bot sent 525 to
  Billing, and Billing closed **1**. Policy §3 says mentioning payment does not make a request Billing.
* **Purifier breakdowns** were sent to Consumables and closed by Repairs.
* **Two requests in one message: the last one decides** (542 of 549 messages, 98.7%).
* **~16% of requests state no need** ("please call me about my purifier"). Their outcomes are spread over all seven
  teams, and no column predicts them. This caps *any* text-only router at ~86%. An oracle that sees the answers
  reaches only 86.25%.
* **~1.6% of clear requests are closed by an unrelated team** at random (recording noise).
* **Data fixes:** team renames merged; legacy Zoho mojibake repaired; legacy resolution times were UTC (26% looked
  "resolved before created"), fixed +5:30; 126 inconsistent records kept and flagged.
* **Headcount:** the bot's labels overstate Repairs (+42/month), Billing (+24) and Consumables (+23), and
  understate Installs (−27), Returns (−25) and Warranty (−22).

## 3. The router

```
message
 └► clean: fix garbled legacy text, merge renamed teams
 └► parse: drop greeting, order no., sign-off, payment remark; the LAST request decides
 └► [B4] wording unknown? fix Hinglish + spelling, read again
     ├─ states no need ─► guess by product (A1, labelled a guess) + 7-option question
     ├─ wording known  ─► team that closed most past requests with that wording (98% right)
     └─ new wording    ─► keyword rules → text model; unsure → clarifying question
 └► output: team · confidence · auto_route (C1) · reasons for the agent · alternatives
unsure requests ─► review queue ─► agent's answer via /feedback ─► learned at next retrain (B5)
```
FastAPI `POST /route` + one screen, `POST /feedback`, `/health`. No API key, no GPU, ~2 s to train, 176 KB model,
worst case 3.7 ms per request. Starts on a clean machine; with no data it still starts and explains what to do.
44 automated tests.

## 4. How it was validated: four rounds

| round | what was tested | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | ~20 approaches on out-of-time, 5-fold CV and held-out wording: TF-IDF variants, embeddings, rules, lookup, local LLM (Qwen2.5-3B) | Lookup + last-request parsing best. The LLM scored 71%, worse than the bot. The copy-the-bot model scored 77% |
| 2 | 11 challengers under a pre-committed protocol, rolling backtest (6,502 predictions), McNemar + Holm: fine-tuned transformer, gradient boosting, kNN, noise cleaning, ensembles | None significantly better; transformer identical on clear requests. Router stayed |
| 3 | Last untested signals (noise pattern, recent context, previous request, time) + operating levers | No exploitable signal. Auto-routing the confident 84% gives 98.4% |
| 4 | 9 engineering ideas as switches, pre-committed protocol | **Adopted:** A1 product-based vague guess (+0.25, labelled a guess), B4 Hinglish/typo repair, B5 corrections loop, C1 auto-route flag. **Rejected:** fuzzy match, paraphrase lookup, 3-way vote (−10 pts), option reordering; embeddings +2.4 but below the bar for adding PyTorch |

**Round 4 effect** (stress tests are synthetic):

| | before round 4 | final |
|---|---|---|
| Real data, out-of-time | 85.7% | **86.0%** |
| Vague requests | 20.2% | **22.0%** |
| Heavy typos (30% of words corrupted) | 94.1% | **97.6%** |
| Hinglish (LLM-rewritten, noisy) | 78.7% | **82.0%** |
| New phrasing after 3 agent-confirmed examples | 89.8% | **98.4%** |

## 5. Where it fails

Out-of-time it is wrong on **299 of 2,135 (14.0%)**:

* **262 vague requests.** Nobody can route these from the text; the router flags them and offers one question.
* **37 clear requests (2.1%)** closed by an unrelated team, mostly records the log itself marks as inconsistent.
* **On live traffic:** genuinely new wording is ~87% right on requests that state a need (range 70–98% by fold),
  so it is flagged when unsure and fed back through the corrections loop.

## 6. Money

Misrouting costs **Rs 14.7 lakh a year** today: 3,129 transfers × Rs 305, plus Rs 260 per repeat contact (policy §4).
Misrouted requests also take twice as long to close (16.6 h vs 8.2 h).
The router cuts wrong-first-team from 23% to 14%, saving **Rs 5.6 lakh**. With the **Rs 3.2 lakh** licence that is
**≈ Rs 8.8 lakh a year**, at **Rs 0 per request**: 700 requests × ~1.5 ms ≈ 1 s of CPU a month.
If the intake question works: up to Rs 16 lakh (projection).

## 7. Recommendation

1. **Switch the bot off after a two-week side-by-side run.** Measure "closed by first team": 77% today, target 86%+.
2. **Pilot the clarifying question on one channel** for vague requests. It is the only lever that can take accuracy
   beyond ~86%, towards ~98%, because it adds the information the message does not contain.
3. **Use real volumes, not bot labels, for headcount.**
4. **Retrain monthly** with agent-confirmed corrections; revisit embeddings if the review queue shows much new
   wording.

## 8. Honest limits

* Tested on history, not live traffic; the export is highly templated (132 distinct phrasings).
* Truth is the resolution log, which is itself ~2% noisy.
* The product-based vague guess (A1) is not statistically proven, is labelled a guess, and costs 0.3 points of
  macro-F1.
* The typo and Hinglish tests are synthetic; the Hinglish set is noisier than real customers.
* The keyword rules were written after reading the data; the fair robustness figure (87%) is the one reported.
* No login or rate limiting on the service; tested on macOS only.
